hits.section: §14 ROLES › Keel
hits.text:
§14 ROLES › Keel
### Keel · Simulation engineer · Opus 5.5
owns: The rulebook: every event in the city, what it needs, what it changes and who sees it. Also the 28 test scenarios and the C# sim library that runs them (Unity-free; provisional, Sky to confirm).
receives: Motive's rules, Waymark's missions, Pulse's schedules, Fable's lines, and what the debrief carries forward.
delivers: The rulebook to everyone; checked content to Latch; mistakes back to their authors. Design decisions stay with Motive.
hold: The rules live apart from the engine. Any run replays exactly from its starting state and the player's orders. One incident counts once toward Alert and dispatches once. Silent acts raise Alert when the report lands. Unity must pass the same 28 scenarios before content goes in. One C# engine: Unity runs it live, tools headless via dotnet; 10 Hz, integer state, replay = orders + checksums. Locked only after the week 4 playtest.
opens: §05, §06, §08, §11

hits.section: Prove the rules small, then dress them › How it's built
hits.text:
Prove the rules small, then dress them › How it's built
The rules live apart from the engine. Everything that happens in the city (a guard leaving, a contact answering) is an event with its conditions, effects and witnesses.
Any run can be replayed exactly from its starting state and the player's orders.
Unity has to pass the same 28 scenarios as the top-down test before it's trusted.
One simulation engine. A Unity-free C# library: Unity runs it live, build tools run it headless. Fixed 10 Hz tick, integer state; a replay is the orders plus checksums.
Performance is judged by frame rate at play zoom, not by polygon counts. The target is 60 fps at 1080p on a 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,13), the reference machine. It has no fan and a 10-core GPU, so it is measured warm, after several minutes of running, at play zoom with people, vehicles and the simulation in, by a perf harness in a development build. A mid-range PC (an RTX 3060-class GPU with a 6-core CPU) must also pass, as a check, not the bar.

hits.section: One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.17.0) (2/2)
hits.text:
One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.17.0)
Budget. Agent work runs inside two existing 20× subscriptions (one Codex, one Claude), which cap usage over time rather than charging per use. Aster watches both and drops optional work when the allowance runs low. Anything paid per use, such as Runware and Meshy credits, is priced before use.
Review record and version history: ../the-suborned-gdd-changelog.html . The Suborned · Game Design Document v0.24.0 · Sky Rumsey · 18 October 2026. Rules tagged Built come from docs/prototypes/suborned-world-sim.js . Values tagged Spec are starting points to be tuned against playtests.

hits.section: §13 TESTS › default
hits.text:
§13 TESTS › default
default: 6 new players.
| id | question | method | pass |
| T1 | tactical pause? | same build, 6 each way | pause wins unless no-pause players explain failures as well and rate tension higher |
| T2 | loud dominates? | log first-shot time + route; re-measured with check-ins and the dial (S2) | < 25% shoot before 2:00; informed quiet runs finish faster |
| T3 | Trail readable? | ask "why is the investigation active?" | ≥ 5/6 give correct cause |
| T4 | witnesses add decisions? | A/B witnesses on/off | players route around crowds on purpose |
| T5 | kidnapping fits tone? | framing survey | cell read as resistance, not criminals |
| T6 | final fight reads as consequence? | ask "why these enemies?" | ≥ 5/6 link it to loud/quiet |
| T7 [L] | contacts memorable? | recall 1 day later | name ≥ 2 contacts + what happened |
| T8 | shoot-outs readable? | ask "why did that operative go down?" | ≥ 5/6 name the cause (outnumbered, no cover, walking, long range) |
| T9 | takedowns cost what they show? | Handover: an unseen takedown route, then the same takedown in front of a witness who reports | the unseen route wins at Alert ≤ 1; the seen one ends in failure or a loud run; ≥ 5/6 say why |
| T10 | the street reads without text? | uncoached, HUD at rest; ask "where is Vale?", "who is the waitress?", "will that walk be seen?" | ≥ 5/6 answer from the scope, the markers and the ring; no capture fails the HUD budget |

hits.section: §11 BUILD › architecture
hits.text:
§11 BUILD › architecture
architecture: rules separate from engine · events carry conditions, effects, witnesses · exact replay from start state + orders · Unity must pass the same 28 scenarios before it's trusted · one C# sim engine as a Unity-free library: Unity runs it live, build tools headless via dotnet; 10 Hz fixed tick, integer state, replay = orders + checksums · performance = frame rate at play zoom, not polygons: target 60 fps at 1080p on the reference machine, a 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (Mac16,13; no fan, 10-core GPU), measured warm (after several minutes of running, since it throttles) at play zoom with people, vehicles and the simulation in, by a perf harness in a development build (Redline specifies it, Latch builds it); a mid-range PC (RTX 3060-class GPU, 6-core CPU) must also pass, as a check, not the bar.

hits.section: Nothing hand-authored, everything checked (3/4)
hits.text:
Nothing hand-authored, everything checked
Consequences | The rules, applied to the mission log | Replaying the mission to confirm the same result |
The mission checker: a generated mission ships only if at least 2 quiet routes win · a loud route exists and costs more Trail · every way to fail can actually happen · no single contact is essential · a player who knows everything finishes with at least a minute to spare. An open case counts as 3 Trail.
The risk is sameness. When everyone is generated, it's easy for nobody to be memorable. Watch Dogs: Legion is the cautionary example. The answer is history, not backstory : people become memorable through what the systems record with you (who you helped, who got braver, who sold you out). Generated text is only a light layer on top. Every fact a person carries must change a price or an outcome: a field that no rule reads is rejected, because detailed bios that change nothing (Legion again) are the opposite of memorable.

hits.section: The city moves without you › The response is a dial Spec
hits.text:
The city moves without you › The response is a dial Spec
"It's easy to swarm the play area with robots if we need to temper the game play" (Sky). How hard a district answers is data per district and mission, not code: the security level is the district's base, plus one for every two open cases (at most two), plus the mission's own bonus. The Handover runs at level 2.
Level | Dispatch | Alert 1 sends | Alert 2+ sends | Another unit every | Unit cap | Seal | Alert 3 adds |
0 · Lax | 20 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 3:00 | — |
1 · Routine | 12 s | 1 robot | 1 unit | — | 1 | 2:25 | — |
2 · Watchful | 10 s | 2 robots | 1 unit + 2 robots | 40 s | 3 | 2:25 | +1 unit, doors lock |
3 · Guarded | 8 s | 2 robots | 2 units + 2 robots | 30 s | 4 | 2:00 | +1 unit, doors lock |
4 · Swarm | 6 s | 3 robots | 2 units + 4 robots | 20 s | 6 | 1:30 | +2 units, doors lock |
A unit is two officers; a robot is an armed patrol unit, and robots count toward the cap of 30 combatants. An alarm sends the response to the scene, then to where the missing person's post, car and closest people are meant to be, then to the people the alarm-raiser knows. Robots only go within 60 m of where they start. Fighting your way out is a last resort, not a route.

hits.section: One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.23.0) (1/4)
hits.text:
One lead, clear owners, named handoffs › Decisions (v0.23.0)
Sky (brief 013): anyone can be targeted, with no list; the cost comes from who sees it. Bodies stay where they fall and are found; the Enforcer carries them to a quiet place, outdoors or through a service door. Both knockout and kill: someone knocked out talks unless hidden, tied up or turned; someone killed never talks, but a found body is far worse. Kills are shown. The cones are the Scout's skill.
Sky, answering Motive: a killing found moves Standing −1, as one value to tune; no rule finds every body, so a hidden one is a missing person (+2 Trail, no Menace, the family and workmates worry; one more guard and camera on that block for 3 missions; every 2 open cases raise the district's security level; a found killing's case closes after 3 missions); the Enforcer's face is a fact a Talker can give up; guards check in every 90 s at times the Scout can learn; a service door and a bin in the lane; the driver can be taken, a missing expected person raises the alarm, and an alarm sends robots and police to the scene and to the connections; the response's size and speed are the difficulty dial, kept as data.

hits.section: The city moves without you › Alert, 0 to 3
hits.text:
The city moves without you › Alert, 0 to 3
Level | Security does | Raised by |
0 · Routine | Follows its schedules | — |
1 · Inquiry | Robots check the reported spot. The patrol tightens its sweep. | A report that lands of a found knockout, a woken victim, a noise, a missed check-in or a missing person; a discovered fault; counted once per incident Spec |
2 · Search | Sends the response unit and robots to the place; their search opens hiding places within 30 m | A second incident; a report that lands of a found kill or a carry seen; any gunfire at once (§06), which sets Alert to at least 2; a shot no longer adds +1 each Built |
3 · Lockdown | Exterior doors lock (security level 2 and up), units cordon the district's mouths, and the district begins to seal. | A report that lands of a takedown seen; gunfire or violence seen by a civilian sets 3 at once Built |
Silent acts wait for the report. A takedown, a carry, a body or a missing person raises Alert only when someone's report reaches security, never at the moment it is seen; gunfire raises it at once, because security hears it. Witness Trail and Standing still move at sight. A knockout that is found, or wakes and reports, never raises Alert above 1; a takedown seen is 3 when it is reported, knockout or not. One takedown is one incident and one dispatch, however many people find it. Spec

Prove the rules small, then dress them › How it's built
The rules live apart from the engine. Everything that happens in the city (a guard leaving, a contact answering) is an event with its conditions, effects and witnesses.
Any run can be replayed exactly from its starting state and the player's orders.

Week | Deliverable | Exit check |
1 | Rules proven in the top-down test | Two routes win, and going loud fails at a cost Done |

3 | Cell control, contacts, security, rivals, readability pass | First uncoached playtest |
4 | Final fight (both branches), payoff cut, Intel, event log, debrief | New-player test; freeze the rules |
